problems.title: Information in retained signal cannot be replaced by information in mask
problems.evidence: X=(Y,Z), independent uniform signs: fixed fullmask has1bit nuisance, zero mask MI; faithfulness holds. Nondegenerate prior-matched mask gives zero KL but0.5bit nuisance.
problems.assumptions: Admissible finite length-two inputs, binary masks and well-defined entropies; semantic condition explicitly checked for fixed masks
problems.counterevidence: Other penalties may aid practical explanation, but do not repair the identity
problems.impact: Invalidates core theoretical derivation, not empirical performance by itself
problems.repair: Keep retained-signal distributions in a valid bound or explicitly relabel mask term as heuristic regularizer
problems.repair_verification: Counterexamples and proper mask variational identity verified; replacement theorem not verified

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Independently read physical p.4 Eqs.(3)-(8) and Appendix B pp.13-15 Eqs.(19)-(33). X=(Y,Z) with independent uniform nonzero signs, binary length-two masks and a classifier depending only on the first coordinate meet the finite-variable setup. Conditional information is evaluated in bits; mask KL in natural-log units.
independent_check.decisive_check: For M=(1,1), conditional on Y the retained signal reveals Z, so I(X;Xm|Y)=H(Z)=1 while I(X;M|Y)=0. For M=(1,0), both are zero. Both retain Y and have exactly matching predictions, excluding the proposed semantic JS condition as a rescue. For independent Bernoulli(.5) mask entries, the mask-prior KL is zero but the erasure channel on Z conveys .5 bit. The map M -> X*M depends on X, so invariance under a fixed invertible map does not apply.
independent_check.interior_parameter_check: To avoid reliance on deterministic Bernoulli endpoints, compare input-independent mask probabilities (.75,.25) and (.75,.75) with prior (.5,.5). All probabilities are strictly interior. Each has equal mask KL=2*[.75 ln(1.5)+.25 ln(.5)], yet retained nuisance information is .25 and .75 bit. The first-coordinate mask distribution is identical, hence every semantic penalty for a classifier of that coordinate has the same expectation. This new analytic strengthening is included in the active report; unlike the deterministic pair it is not claimed to have perfect fidelity.
independent_check.counterevidence: The mask-only variational identity is valid and regularization can help empirically. The independent random-mask example isolates the regularizer, not the perfect-fidelity constraint. Neither fact recovers the retained-value identity or optimization equivalence.
independent_check.dependency_severity_repair: Major retained because the paper explicitly derives its central nuisance-information objective via the non-equivalent substitution. Retain distributions of Xm in an actual bound or label the mask KL a heuristic prior regularizer; no replacement objective guarantee verified.
independent_check.other_reported_subfindings: X=(Y,Y),M=(1,0) verifies retained sufficiency while the physically removed complement still has one bit about Y; source removal language needs this boundary. Eq.(31) chain rule holds. Eq.(32) marginal similarity alone is inadequate, and the no-nuisance assumption is separately asserted, not derived. Eq.(33) uses input-dependent inverse-mask negatives, so no standard independent-marginal MI lower bound has been established; no claim is made that its empirical surrogate cannot work.

problems.title: Released temperature hook does not implement the stated backward softmax
problems.evidence: Fixed-temperature Jacobians0.0350 vs0.0747; noise scaling gives different hard choices
problems.assumptions: Adaptation rate zero isolates permitted fixed-temperature subcase; unequal positive temperatures
problems.counterevidence: Equal temperatures coincide; original run version/configuration unavailable
problems.impact: Release differs from pseudocode; historical performance impact Needs Evidence
problems.repair: Specify one estimator and align gradient/noise computation before re-evaluation
problems.repair_verification: Independent formula checks only; no author program execution

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Read the physical p.15 Algorithm 1 image and maskgen.py:67-100 statically. Adaptation rate zero is allowed and removes temperature-gradient dependencies; choose positive unequal temperatures within clipping bounds.
independent_check.decisive_check: With l=(1,-1),g=0,tauf=1,taub=3, the hook multiplies the derivative through zf=(l+g)/tauf by tauf/taub, yielding J(softmax(l))/3. Its diagonal is exp(2)/(1+exp(2))^2/3 about .034998. Algorithm 1 instead yields J(softmax(l/3))/3, diagonal about .074719. With g=(-.4,.4), dividing l by tau before adding g flips the preferred index from 1 to 2 as tau changes 1 to 3; dividing l+g by a positive tau does not. Strict inequality persists for an open set of Gumbel noise, so this is not only a measure-zero equality example.
independent_check.counterevidence: Equal temperatures remove the backward-shape discrepancy for matched noise conventions, but do not generally resolve the separately different placement of noise scaling. Source lines constructing a backward softmax are commented out. Exact historical configuration is unknown and no source program ran.
independent_check.dependency_severity_repair: Minor release/specification discrepancy, separate from P1 theoretical Major. Choose one forward/backward estimator, implement its intended Jacobian and noise scaling, then evaluate it. No trained-model repair or measured benchmark effect is asserted.
independent_check.protocol_scope: consistency.py:320-339 explicitly selects checkpoints by explanation AUPRC when test is supplied. Missing caller/split evidence prevents determining whether this argument is a held-out test set or an independent validation set; retain Needs Evidence rather than declaring leakage.
